record.paper_title: Some Open Problems of Ramsey Minimal Graphs
record.original_question: For each integer n ≥ 4, characterize all graphs F that are Ramsey (2K₂, 2Pₙ)-minimal; that is, every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of 2K₂ or a blue copy of 2Pₙ, but for every edge e of F the graph F − e has some red-blue coloring with neither a red copy of 2K₂ nor a blue copy of 2Pₙ.

evidence.quote: say that \(F \rightarrow (G, H)\) if whenever the edges of \(F\) are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of \(G\) or a blue copy of \(H\). A graph \(F\) is called Ramsey \((G, H)\)-minimal if \(F \rightarrow (G, H)\) but for any edge \(e \in E(F)\), we have \((F - e) \nrightarrow (G, H)\).
More specifically, these problems consider the case where \(G = 2K\_{2}\), the matching on 2 edges.

evidence.page: zbMATH review body, Problem 2 third clause
evidence.quote: For each \(n \geq 4\), characterize the graphs in \(\mathfrak{R}(2K\_{2}, 2P\_{n})\).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G and H be simple graphs. For a simple graph F, write F → (G, H) if for every red-blue coloring of the edges of F there is either a monochromatic red subgraph isomorphic to G or a monochromatic blue subgraph isomorphic to H. A graph F is said to be Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) and, for every edge e ∈ E(F), the graph F − e does not satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let R(G, H) denote the class of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs (considered up to isomorphism).

Denote by 2K₂ the matching consisting of two disjoint edges, by Pₙ the path on n vertices, and by 2Pₙ the disjoint union of two copies of Pₙ.

Problem. For each integer n ≥ 4, give an explicit characterization of all graphs F belonging to R(2K₂, 2Pₙ).
artifact.status_search_result: Complete characterizations of R(2K₂, 2Pₙ) have been obtained for small n (notably n = 3, 4, 5) by Tatanto and Baskoro, and structural results are known (the only disconnected members are 3Pₙ and unions F∪G with F,G connected members of R(2K₂, Pₙ)). A full characterization for all n ≥ 4 does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem appears to be partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey minimal graphs for 2K2 versus Pn
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of R(2K2, Pn) for n=4,5 by Baskoro and Yulianti; structural results on R(2K2, 2Pn).
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterizations are known for small n; general case is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (mK2, P4)-minimal graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses known characterizations including R(2K2,2Pn) for small n.
status_evidence.claim: Cases n=4,5 of R(2K2,2Pn) have been characterized; general n remains open.
